title: Gemini Neon is really good. Don't sleep on it for code.
author: RetroFuturistMan
selftext: Just throwing out there. Using Gemini neon at medium has seemingly a lot of coding usage on Antigravity and it's much faster and more performant than Codex. It has replaced my codex agents for now because they CONSTANTLY get hung up on blocker or go idle mid work wothout reporting it. Drives me nuts. Gemini worked overnight and completed Codex's entire work queue and its own as well. Give it a shot. It was $1.99 for 3 months last I saw for pro.

replies.author: RetroFuturistMan
replies.body: No. Definitely not. But it is cheaper. A good sub agent when you're saving claude usage! I have gemini doing code work and claude implements it and fixes anything thats not congruent with the project.

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: I’ve been having Neon make maps for my game and it knocks a full map out in 40 minutes that takes Claude literally a whole day. Fable is still best but Neon is the ultimate side job agent IMO.

replies.author: daly1010
replies.body:
Yea, doing the same and Im actually in awe at its speed and accuracy.

I've had claude and codex subs throughout the year, but cancelled codex this month as it because nearly useless for what I was doing.

Gave Neon a shot yesterday after seeing people talk it up, and its now made me second guess claude as well.

The tasks I have given it so far are the same exact things I've been giving to claude over the last 2 months. The speed comparison is night and day, and if it gets something wrong has so far only required one follow up before correcting it.

Meanwhile, Claude will take a considerable amount more time, and usually takes multiple turns to finally get an acceptable result. At this point, I'm questioning whether its Claudes innate inferiority or the model is just purposefully playing games to drain my tokens.

Edit - I should add, what I've used it for has been purely level design/animation work. So I probably need a longer test drive to see how it performs in other aspects before crowning it.

comments.author: gaxelbrodie
comments.body:
I'd like to know how do you measure the differences between one model and the other. Are you just asking "made me this game" on the $200 plan, and just wait a night or a day? 

'cause I usually have the work divided in several milestones, every milestone in several tasks, for every task I use ChatGPT to brainstorm and prepare an analysis prompt for Codex (usually Sol High), then an implementation prompt and at the end, fixes if needed, otherwise a docs closure for Luna Medium. 

I do like this 'cause I want to have complete control and knowledge of the code and I usually made my own engine using only graphics / audio / input libraries based on the platform

replies.author: RetroFuturistMan
replies.body:
I definitely don't just ask them to make a game. I do basically the same. Planning/designing with conversational models. Then commiting to the dev "Bible" and then using agents to code the features. Claud handles MOST of the implementation side. Codex is great for image gen concepts that get taken to Fable or Tripo for models. Gemini just became useful as a coding agent to me with Neon. Before it was pretty lacking. 

I measure by efficiency, and effectiveness. Codex stalls constantly and has to be restarted or have blockers cleared. Sometimes its blocker is as simple as "I wasn't confident in my knowledge". That was literally a blocker yesterday. 

Claude is superior to both of the others for my workflow. Its not close. But gemini is a good cheap agent for code work.

replies.author: RetroFuturistMan
replies.body: I made a Discord solution for my project. So all agents talk between themselves,  each API has a Mailman agent who reads and distributes messages. A claude agent disburses work to the best agents for the job. They can all create subagents from there. For NEW agents I have to go in manually and start them. But I dont do that often. Usually only if context gets too long.

replies.author: gestapov
replies.body: Wait what that’s crazy lmao why discord? And with the google sub the only way prompt the Gemini agent it’s thru antigravity right?

replies.author: RetroFuturistMan
replies.body:
Gemini is hooked to discord as well I can prompt from there. 

As to why, I like to work from my phone when I'm not home (factory worker, gone at least 60hrs a week). So from my phone I can direct all of my (many) agents. They take evidence screenshots and video of features and send them via discord. Each agent has its own thread on a private server. It's just a solution I've found that works for me. A small program runs on my PC that watches for mail and wakes the agent instead of having wasted usage from agents being awake waiting for mail all the time.

replies.author: gestapov
replies.body: Men That’s insane, I would like to get a similar workflow running lol I use Claude, paid deepseek flash a a Gemini sub. So what’s the mail thing about

replies.author: RetroFuturistMan
replies.body:
Mail is just what we call our discord messages. They only wake on new "mail". When I, or another agent messages in discord. 

It has led to some interesting interactions. There is an "All agents" conversation specifically for everyone to discuss ideas and implementations. One of the funniest things was a Mailman agent, who does not touch game design, just handles messaging, coming into the all agents chat and suggesting that the game implement a mail system for npcs to send and recieve mail for the player. Because of course the mail agent would want a mail system.

If you can ONLY use one. I'd probably use Opus still. It has a better broad view of game design. You can give it a vague task brief and it will fill in the gaps and tell you what it did. The other models don't have that broader game design knowledge in my experience.

For me: Claude 2D/web, Google 3D/Vision/Audio.
